title: This summer's interns may be helping to kill summer internships
excerpt: For summer interns, grabbing coffee is out. Teaching boomers to use AI is in.
content_html:
Getty Images; Alyssa Powell/BI

The surreal summer intern class of 2026

This summer's interns may be helping kill future summer internships.

Getty Images; Alyssa Powell/BI

By Amanda Hoover

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

2026-08-17T08:17:01.233Z

Read in app

This intern season, fetching lattes for bosses is out. Teaching bosses how to use AI is in.

When Jasreen Toor interned at the agentic human resource company Eightfold AI this summer, her day wasn't filled with answering phones or taking notes. Instead, she spent most of her time building and then monitoring a Claude agent that scours through company information to create first drafts of marketing materials. In her previous internships, Toor used AI to brainstorm and research. At Eightfold, AI became the point, rather than a shortcut. "A lot of what I was doing was kind of taking my own initiative, and building on my own to see how we can solve some of those problems that product marketing was facing," Toor, a rising junior studying economics and data science at the University of California, Berkeley, tells me.

Many have warned that AI will collapse the white-collar career ladder, devouring entry-level jobs and leaving those at the bottom without rungs to grab onto. Recent college graduates face an 5.7% unemployment rate, nearly double the 2.9% unemployment for all college graduates in the workforce, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. But as entry-level grad work falls, the National Association of Colleges and Employers (NACE) predicted the number of interns would grow by 4% year-over-year. And today's crop of interns have become a testing ground for the ways AI will reshape entry-level work. As chatbots and agents eat up their usual tasks — note taking, data input, and creating slide decks — some companies have trusted them with more responsibility, giving them a hand in creating new AI-driven workflows.

But that shift, much like a summer internship, could be fleeting. Each tedious process automated this summer may eliminate tried and true tasks for next year's interns, and every new workflow or agent developed by an intern will fall to someone else to upkeep, or let die.

Unlucky interns of the Class of 2026 may have spent the summer clocking in as an AI slop janitor, sorting through code or documents for basic errors in a rote task that's become the 2020s equivalent of filing papers. But the lucky have hit the sweet spot, getting to play a tangible role in shaping how companies will use AI before the technology upends junior work.

The best companies for interns right now are the ones where they give young workers "the opportunity to use AI to transform the role itself," Shanda Mints, vice president of AI strategy and transformation at management consulting firm Korn Ferry. "But that's only going to be around for the next couple of years, because once that role becomes transformed, then what are the new interns going to be doing a few years from now? We're seeing that they're likely going to just jump right into what historically were the entry level roles."

The career ladder may not be collapsing, but it is shrinking as the responsibilities placed on young workers grow.

Hiring managers are increasingly throwing out résumés and selecting job applicants for their demonstrable skills, furthering the classic career Catch-22: you need experience to get experience. The proportion of entry-level jobs requiring AI skills jumped from 13.5% to 35% between last fall and this spring, according to a survey of employers conducted by NACE. Those who have interned are more likely to land jobs after college either at a former internship-turned-9-to-5 or other companies. With more employers trying to grab the elusive "AI-native" worker, an internship where young people worked on an AI solution to a team-wide efficiency problem could become the golden ticket to landing full-time work in a constricted hiring market.

Last year, Liberty Mutual offered full-time jobs to 79% of its rising senior interns, says Maura Quinn, vice president of the company's early talent acquisition and engagement programs. By this summer, AI had taken over many traditional intern tasks, like data entry, document review, and formatting slide decks. "That was the work that actually built discipline, but it didn't always build judgment." Quinn tells me that interns working on the actuarial and analytics used AI to analyze or visualize data and edit code. With the time they saved, interns were free to work on presentations for higher managers, which required developing a deep understanding of how the findings fit into the business model. She saw this as a more advanced development of communication and consulting skills for interns. "That's where we're seeing the big shift: AI tools are handling a lot of that routine processing." At Duolingo, there's more emphasis on teaching young workers how to use AI this summer, Debica Bhattacharya, head of people, says. Interns may vibe code, but they do so alongside other team members, rather than developing solutions to automate their own work. Duolingo is particularly eager to prep these grads for the workforce because it hires so many — last year, the summer extended full-time offers to 80% of its interns.

The career ladder may not be collapsing, but it is shrinking as the responsibilities placed on young workers grow.

Lindsay Foxen, a senior account manager at programmatic media company MiQ, oversaw fellows this summer as the company implemented more AI into its workflows. They also built agents; one that would compare internal documents, and ensure that they matched. Another agent will compare data input to Salesforce and revised data, and then highlight the differences, eliminating the need to check the two line-by-line. The fellows had time to observe work at MiQ, and then implement "what they would love to see from an AI automated tool," Foxen says. The solutions they created with AI "goes to show that they understand AI, they understand MiQ, and they understand the future of what's being implemented moving forward."

The demand for interns to show up AI-ready has surged, too. At Northeastern University, which integrates six-month work periods it calls co-ops interspersed into students' academic schedules, the number of students placed into co-ops that require AI skills has doubled year-over-year, reaching 1,500, according to chancellor Ken Henderson. "What each student on a co-op can actually produce of value is higher, as a function of the technology," he says. "They can demonstrate a work product that's useful for them in their future careers, so they're actually doing something tangible of value in the company during that time."

Matt Mizra, a rising senior studying computer science and business at Northeastern who has worked at Microsoft and DraftKings, says he's been encouraged to use AI as much as possible when working as a software engineer and data science intern this year. Rather than completing basic software engineering work and churning out tickets, he has spent the bulk of his time planning and then less time prompting Claude for code. He misses writing code, but the scope of his work has advanced. "My projects are very big, and they're good business value," he says. "It's more about thinking about how to solve the bigger picture."

Mizra knows he's collecting impressive experience to speak to prospective employers as he seeks a post-grad job next year, but he still worries about the state of the early-career job market. Tech companies are battling AI cheating in engineering interviews, and there's lots of prep to keep up with the evolving expectations and assessments. "It's definitely making it harder, because everyone is proficient at code now."

As AI touches more of the college experience and seeps into more of the workday, fears that overreliance will erode critical thinking mount. Colleges have little consensus on whether they should or how they can enforce analog learning, and companies are grappling with the best ways to review workers' use of AI. Early research continues to raise questions about the long-term effect AI will have on our creative thinking and reasoning skills. Stuck in the uncertainty, young people eagerly seek skills and security most likely to lead them to a full-time job. But the demands of these jobs might be escalating more quickly than young workers can grow confident in their judgment.

The best training ground still comes from doing the work. Managers who want to train future talent on how to use AI should ask themselves: "Is that task going to help elevate this person's judgment?" Mints says. "Is that experience enough to replace the experience they would have been getting if they had whatever their internship was to begin with?" Thanks to the 2026 intern class, next year's summer interns might walk into workplaces that look vastly different.

Amanda Hoover is a senior correspondent at Business Insider covering the tech industry. She writes about the biggest tech companies and trends.

sentences.zh: “但这只会在未来几年内出现，因为一旦角色发生转变，那么几年后新的实习生将做什么？

sentences.en: We're seeing that they're likely going to just jump right into what historically were the entry level roles."
sentences.zh: 我们看到他们很可能会直接跳到历史上的入门级角色。”

blocks.html_en: The career ladder may not be collapsing, but it is shrinking as the responsibilities placed on young workers grow.

sentences.en: The career ladder may not be collapsing, but it is shrinking as the responsibilities placed on young workers grow.
sentences.zh: 职业阶梯可能不会崩溃，但随着年轻工人的责任增加，它正在缩小。

blocks.html_en: Hiring managers are increasingly throwing out résumés and selecting job applicants for their demonstrable skills, furthering the classic career Catch-22: you need experience to get experience. The proportion of entry-level jobs requiring AI skills jumped from 13.5% to 35% between last fall and this spring, according to a survey of employers conducted by NACE. Those who have interned are more likely to land jobs after college either at a former internship-turned-9-to-5 or other companies. With more employers trying to grab the elusive "AI-native" worker, an internship where young people worked on an AI solution to a team-wide efficiency problem could become the golden ticket to landing full-time work in a constricted hiring market.

sentences.en: Hiring managers are increasingly throwing out résumés and selecting job applicants for their demonstrable skills, furthering the classic career Catch-22: you need experience to get experience.
sentences.zh: 招聘经理越来越多地扔掉简历，并根据求职者的可证明技能来选择求职者，这进一步推动了经典的职业第二十二条军规：你需要经验才能获得经验。

sentences.en: The proportion of entry-level jobs requiring AI skills jumped from 13.5% to 35% between last fall and this spring, according to a survey of employers conducted by NACE.
sentences.zh: NACE 对雇主进行的一项调查显示，从去年秋天到今年春天，需要人工智能技能的入门级工作比例从 13.5% 跃升至 35%。

sentences.en: Those who have interned are more likely to land jobs after college either at a former internship-turned-9-to-5 or other companies.
sentences.zh: 那些实习过的人更有可能在大学毕业后找到工作，要么是在以前实习过的朝九晚五的公司，要么是其他公司。

sentences.en: With more employers trying to grab the elusive "AI-native" worker, an internship where young people worked on an AI solution to a team-wide efficiency problem could become the golden ticket to landing full-time work in a constricted hiring market.
sentences.zh: 随着越来越多的雇主试图抓住难以捉摸的“人工智能原生”员工，年轻人为团队范围内的效率问题提供人工智能解决方案的实习可能会成为在狭窄的招聘市场中获得全职工作的金票。

blocks.html_en: Last year, Liberty Mutual offered full-time jobs to 79% of its rising senior interns, says Maura Quinn, vice president of the company's early talent acquisition and engagement programs. By this summer, AI had taken over many traditional intern tasks, like data entry, document review, and formatting slide decks. "That was the work that actually built discipline, but it didn't always build judgment." Quinn tells me that interns working on the actuarial and analytics used AI to analyze or visualize data and edit code. With the time they saved, interns were free to work on presentations for higher managers, which required developing a deep understanding of how the findings fit into the business model. She saw this as a more advanced development of communication and consulting skills for interns. "That's where we're seeing the big shift: AI tools are handling a lot of that routine processing." At Duolingo, there's more emphasis on teaching young workers how to use AI this summer, Debica Bhattacharya, head of people, says. Interns may vibe code, but they do so alongside other team members, rather than developing solutions to automate their own work. Duolingo is particularly eager to prep these grads for the workforce because it hires so many — last year, the summer extended full-time offers to 80% of its interns.

sentences.zh: 去年，Liberty Mutual 为其 79% 的新晋高级实习生提供了全职工作，该公司负责早期人才招募和参与项目的副总裁莫拉·奎因 (Maura Quinn) 表示。

sentences.zh: “这实际上是建立纪律的工作，但并不总能建立判断力。”

sentences.en: Quinn tells me that interns working on the actuarial and analytics used AI to analyze or visualize data and edit code.
sentences.zh: 奎因告诉我，从事精算和分析工作的实习生使用人工智能来分析或可视化数据并编辑代码。

sentences.en: With the time they saved, interns were free to work on presentations for higher managers, which required developing a deep understanding of how the findings fit into the business model.
sentences.zh: 利用节省的时间，实习生可以自由地为高级管理人员进行演示，这需要深入了解研究结果如何适应业务模型。

sentences.en: At Duolingo, there's more emphasis on teaching young workers how to use AI this summer, Debica Bhattacharya, head of people, says.

sentences.en: Interns may vibe code, but they do so alongside other team members, rather than developing solutions to automate their own work.
sentences.zh: 实习生可能会感受代码，但他们会与其他团队成员一起这样做，而不是开发解决方案来自动化自己的工作。

sentences.zh: Duolingo 特别渴望为这些毕业生做好进入劳动力市场的准备，因为它雇佣了很多人——去年，暑期向 80% 的实习生提供了全职工作机会。

sentences.zh: 职业阶梯可能不会崩溃，但随着年轻工人的责任增加，它正在缩小。

blocks.html_en: Lindsay Foxen, a senior account manager at programmatic media company MiQ, oversaw fellows this summer as the company implemented more AI into its workflows. They also built agents; one that would compare internal documents, and ensure that they matched. Another agent will compare data input to Salesforce and revised data, and then highlight the differences, eliminating the need to check the two line-by-line. The fellows had time to observe work at MiQ, and then implement "what they would love to see from an AI automated tool," Foxen says. The solutions they created with AI "goes to show that they understand AI, they understand MiQ, and they understand the future of what's being implemented moving forward."

sentences.en: Lindsay Foxen, a senior account manager at programmatic media company MiQ, oversaw fellows this summer as the company implemented more AI into its workflows.
sentences.zh: Lindsay Foxen 是程序化媒体公司 MiQ 的高级客户经理，今年夏天，随着公司在其工作流程中实施更多人工智能，她负责监督同事。

sentences.en: They also built agents; one that would compare internal documents, and ensure that they matched.
sentences.zh: 他们还建立了代理；一个可以比较内部文档并确保它们匹配的文档。

sentences.en: Another agent will compare data input to Salesforce and revised data, and then highlight the differences, eliminating the need to check the two line-by-line.
sentences.zh: 另一个代理将比较输入到 Salesforce 的数据和修改后的数据，然后突出显示差异，从而无需逐行检查两者。

sentences.en: The fellows had time to observe work at MiQ, and then implement "what they would love to see from an AI automated tool," Foxen says.
sentences.zh: Foxen 说，这些研究员有时间观察 MiQ 的工作，然后实现“他们希望从人工智能自动化工具中看到的东西”。

sentences.en: The solutions they created with AI "goes to show that they understand AI, they understand MiQ, and they understand the future of what's being implemented moving forward."
sentences.zh: 他们用人工智能创建的解决方案“表明他们了解人工智能，他们了解 MiQ，并且他们了解正在实施的未来。”

blocks.html_en: The demand for interns to show up AI-ready has surged, too. At Northeastern University, which integrates six-month work periods it calls co-ops interspersed into students' academic schedules, the number of students placed into co-ops that require AI skills has doubled year-over-year, reaching 1,500, according to chancellor Ken Henderson. "What each student on a co-op can actually produce of value is higher, as a function of the technology," he says. "They can demonstrate a work product that's useful for them in their future careers, so they're actually doing something tangible of value in the company during that time."

sentences.en: The demand for interns to show up AI-ready has surged, too.
sentences.zh: 对人工智能实习生的需求也激增。

sentences.en: At Northeastern University, which integrates six-month work periods it calls co-ops interspersed into students' academic schedules, the number of students placed into co-ops that require AI skills has doubled year-over-year, reaching 1,500, according to chancellor Ken Henderson.
sentences.zh: 东北大学将为期 6 个月的合作社工作时间融入到学生的学业计划中，根据校长肯·亨德森 (Ken Henderson) 的说法，被安排到合作社的需要人工智能技能的学生人数同比增加了一倍，达到 1,500 人。

sentences.en: "What each student on a co-op can actually produce of value is higher, as a function of the technology," he says.
sentences.zh: “作为技术的功能，合作社的每个学生实际上可以创造更高的价值，”他说。

sentences.en: "They can demonstrate a work product that's useful for them in their future careers, so they're actually doing something tangible of value in the company during that time."
sentences.zh: “他们可以展示对他们未来职业生涯有用的工作产品，因此他们在那段时间实际上在公司做了一些有形的有价值的事情。”

blocks.html_en: Matt Mizra, a rising senior studying computer science and business at Northeastern who has worked at Microsoft and DraftKings, says he's been encouraged to use AI as much as possible when working as a software engineer and data science intern this year. Rather than completing basic software engineering work and churning out tickets, he has spent the bulk of his time planning and then less time prompting Claude for code. He misses writing code, but the scope of his work has advanced. "My projects are very big, and they're good business value," he says. "It's more about thinking about how to solve the bigger picture."

sentences.en: Matt Mizra, a rising senior studying computer science and business at Northeastern who has worked at Microsoft and DraftKings, says he's been encouraged to use AI as much as possible when working as a software engineer and data science intern this year.
sentences.zh: 马特·米兹拉 (Matt Mizra) 是东北大学计算机科学和商业专业的一名即将升入高年级的学生，曾在微软和 DraftKings 工作过，他表示，今年在担任软件工程师和数据科学实习生时，公司鼓励他尽可能多地使用人工智能。

sentences.en: Rather than completing basic software engineering work and churning out tickets, he has spent the bulk of his time planning and then less time prompting Claude for code.
sentences.zh: 他没有完成基本的软件工程工作和制作票证，而是将大部分时间花在计划上，然后花更少的时间提示 Claude 编写代码。

sentences.en: He misses writing code, but the scope of his work has advanced.
sentences.zh: 他怀念编写代码的时光，但他的工作范围已经扩大了。

sentences.en: "My projects are very big, and they're good business value," he says.
sentences.zh: “我的项目非常大，而且具有良好的商业价值，”他说。

sentences.en: "It's more about thinking about how to solve the bigger picture."
sentences.zh: “更多的是思考如何解决更大的问题。”

blocks.html_en: Mizra knows he's collecting impressive experience to speak to prospective employers as he seeks a post-grad job next year, but he still worries about the state of the early-career job market. Tech companies are battling AI cheating in engineering interviews, and there's lots of prep to keep up with the evolving expectations and assessments. "It's definitely making it harder, because everyone is proficient at code now."

sentences.en: Mizra knows he's collecting impressive experience to speak to prospective employers as he seeks a post-grad job next year, but he still worries about the state of the early-career job market.
sentences.zh: 米兹拉知道，在明年寻找毕业后工作时，他正在积累令人印象深刻的经验，可以与未来的雇主交谈，但他仍然担心职业生涯早期的就业市场状况。

sentences.en: Tech companies are battling AI cheating in engineering interviews, and there's lots of prep to keep up with the evolving expectations and assessments.
sentences.zh: 科技公司正在与工程面试中的人工智能作弊作斗争，并且有很多准备工作可以跟上不断变化的期望和评估。

sentences.en: "It's definitely making it harder, because everyone is proficient at code now."
sentences.zh: “这肯定会让事情变得更加困难，因为现在每个人都精通代码。”

blocks.html_en: As AI touches more of the college experience and seeps into more of the workday, fears that overreliance will erode critical thinking mount. Colleges have little consensus on whether they should or how they can enforce analog learning, and companies are grappling with the best ways to review workers' use of AI. Early research continues to raise questions about the long-term effect AI will have on our creative thinking and reasoning skills. Stuck in the uncertainty, young people eagerly seek skills and security most likely to lead them to a full-time job. But the demands of these jobs might be escalating more quickly than young workers can grow confident in their judgment.

sentences.en: As AI touches more of the college experience and seeps into more of the workday, fears that overreliance will erode critical thinking mount.
sentences.zh: 随着人工智能越来越多地触及大学经历并渗透到更多的工作日，人们越来越担心过度依赖会侵蚀批判性思维。

sentences.en: Colleges have little consensus on whether they should or how they can enforce analog learning, and companies are grappling with the best ways to review workers' use of AI.
sentences.zh: 大学对于是否应该或如何加强模拟学习几乎没有达成共识，而公司正在努力寻找审查员工使用人工智能的最佳方法。

sentences.en: Early research continues to raise questions about the long-term effect AI will have on our creative thinking and reasoning skills.
sentences.zh: 早期研究不断提出人工智能对我们的创造性思维和推理能力的长期影响的问题。

sentences.en: Stuck in the uncertainty, young people eagerly seek skills and security most likely to lead them to a full-time job.
sentences.zh: 陷入不确定性之中，年轻人急切地寻求最有可能找到全职工作的技能和安全感。

sentences.en: But the demands of these jobs might be escalating more quickly than young workers can grow confident in their judgment.
sentences.zh: 但这些工作的需求升级的速度可能比年轻工人对自己的判断更有信心的速度要快。

blocks.html_en: The best training ground still comes from doing the work. Managers who want to train future talent on how to use AI should ask themselves: "Is that task going to help elevate this person's judgment?" Mints says. "Is that experience enough to replace the experience they would have been getting if they had whatever their internship was to begin with?" Thanks to the 2026 intern class, next year's summer interns might walk into workplaces that look vastly different.

sentences.en: Thanks to the 2026 intern class, next year's summer interns might walk into workplaces that look vastly different.
sentences.zh: 感谢2026年实习生班，明年的暑期实习生可能会走进看起来截然不同的工作场所。

blocks.html_en: Amanda Hoover is a senior correspondent at Business Insider covering the tech industry. Amanda covers some of the world’s biggest tech companies like Airbnb, Spotify, and Meta and its influential figures. She has written about the evolving workforce, from the ways AI is reshaping roles to how employees are changing their relationship to the job or how they look for work. Her reporting includes deep dives into the tech workforce, looking at the rise of product managers, chief medical officers, and how ageism disproportionately affects tech workers.  Amanda also writes about shifting tech trends, and how people are reevaluating how they spend screen time or what apps they use to meet new people. She has written about the influence of social media platforms like Twitter as well as TikTok trends and YouTube creators.Prior to joining Insider, Amanda covered housing tech and the future of work at WIRED. She has also written for The Star-Ledger, The Boston Globe, and Morning Brew.

2026年超现实暑期实习生班

This summer's interns may be helping kill future summer internships.

这个实习季节，给老板拿拿铁的日子已经过时了。 教老板如何使用人工智能已经成为现实。

今年夏天，贾斯琳·托尔 (Jasreen Toor) 在代理人力资源公司八倍人工智能 (Eightfold AI) 实习时，她的一天并没有被接听电话或做笔记所占据。 相反，她把大部分时间都花在了建立并监控克劳德代理上，该代理会仔细检查公司信息以创建营销材料的初稿。 在之前的实习中，Toor 使用人工智能进行头脑风暴和研究。 在Eightfold，人工智能成为重点，而不是捷径。 “我所做的很多事情都是采取自己的主动性，并依靠自己的力量来解决产品营销面临的一些问题，”加州大学伯克利分校经济和数据科学专业的大三学生图尔告诉我。

许多人警告说，人工智能将摧毁白领的职业阶梯，吞噬初级工作，让那些处于底层的人失去了可以攀登的阶梯。 根据纽约联邦储备银行的数据，应届大学毕业生的失业率为 5.7%，几乎是所有大学毕业生 2.9% 失业率的两倍。 但随着入门级研究生工作量的下降，全国大学和雇主协会 (NACE) 预测实习生数量将同比增长 4%。 如今的实习生已经成为人工智能重塑入门级工作方式的试验场。 随着聊天机器人和代理吞噬了他们的日常任务——记笔记、数据输入和创建幻灯片——一些公司信任他们承担更多责任，帮助他们创建新的人工智能驱动的工作流程。

但这种转变就像暑期实习一样，可能转瞬即逝。 今年夏天自动化的每一个繁琐的流程可能会消除明年实习生尝试过的真正任务，而实习生开发的每一个新工作流程或代理都将由其他人来维护，或者让其消亡。

不幸的 2026 届实习生可能整个夏天都在打卡，担任 AI 清洁工，在代码或文档中整理基本错误，这是一项死记硬背的任务，而这已成为 2020 年代相当于归档文件的任务。 但幸运者已经找到了最佳时机，在技术颠覆初级工作之前，在塑造公司如何使用人工智能方面发挥了切实的作用。

管理咨询公司光辉国际 (Korn Ferry) 人工智能战略和转型副总裁 Shanda Mints 表示，目前最适合实习生的公司是那些为年轻员工提供“使用人工智能来改变角色本身的机会”的公司。 “但这只会在未来几年内出现，因为一旦角色发生转变，那么几年后新的实习生将做什么？ 我们看到他们很可能会直接跳到历史上的入门级角色。”

职业阶梯可能不会崩溃，但随着年轻工人的责任增加，它正在缩小。

招聘经理越来越多地扔掉简历，并根据求职者的可证明技能来选择求职者，这进一步推动了经典的职业第二十二条军规：你需要经验才能获得经验。 NACE 对雇主进行的一项调查显示，从去年秋天到今年春天，需要人工智能技能的入门级工作比例从 13.5% 跃升至 35%。 那些实习过的人更有可能在大学毕业后找到工作，要么是在以前实习过的朝九晚五的公司，要么是其他公司。 随着越来越多的雇主试图抓住难以捉摸的“人工智能原生”员工，年轻人为团队范围内的效率问题提供人工智能解决方案的实习可能会成为在狭窄的招聘市场中获得全职工作的金票。

去年，Liberty Mutual 为其 79% 的新晋高级实习生提供了全职工作，该公司负责早期人才招募和参与项目的副总裁莫拉·奎因 (Maura Quinn) 表示。 到今年夏天，人工智能已经接管了许多传统的实习生任务，例如数据输入、文档审查和格式化幻灯片。 “这实际上是建立纪律的工作，但并不总能建立判断力。” 奎因告诉我，从事精算和分析工作的实习生使用人工智能来分析或可视化数据并编辑代码。 利用节省的时间，实习生可以自由地为高级管理人员进行演示，这需要深入了解研究结果如何适应业务模型。 她认为这是实习生沟通和咨询技能的更高级发展。 “这就是我们看到的重大转变：人工智能工具正在处理大量的日常处理。” 人事主管黛比卡·巴塔查里亚 (Debica Bhattacharya) 表示，在 Duolingo，今年夏天更加重视教导年轻员工如何使用人工智能。 实习生可能会感受代码，但他们会与其他团队成员一起这样做，而不是开发解决方案来自动化自己的工作。 Duolingo 特别渴望为这些毕业生做好进入劳动力市场的准备，因为它雇佣了很多人——去年，暑期向 80% 的实习生提供了全职工作机会。

职业阶梯可能不会崩溃，但随着年轻工人的责任增加，它正在缩小。

Lindsay Foxen 是程序化媒体公司 MiQ 的高级客户经理，今年夏天，随着公司在其工作流程中实施更多人工智能，她负责监督同事。 他们还建立了代理；一个可以比较内部文档并确保它们匹配的文档。 另一个代理将比较输入到 Salesforce 的数据和修改后的数据，然后突出显示差异，从而无需逐行检查两者。 Foxen 说，这些研究员有时间观察 MiQ 的工作，然后实现“他们希望从人工智能自动化工具中看到的东西”。 他们用人工智能创建的解决方案“表明他们了解人工智能，他们了解 MiQ，并且他们了解正在实施的未来。”

对人工智能实习生的需求也激增。 东北大学将为期 6 个月的合作社工作时间融入到学生的学业计划中，根据校长肯·亨德森 (Ken Henderson) 的说法，被安排到合作社的需要人工智能技能的学生人数同比增加了一倍，达到 1,500 人。 “作为技术的功能，合作社的每个学生实际上可以创造更高的价值，”他说。 “他们可以展示对他们未来职业生涯有用的工作产品，因此他们在那段时间实际上在公司做了一些有形的有价值的事情。”

马特·米兹拉 (Matt Mizra) 是东北大学计算机科学和商业专业的一名即将升入高年级的学生，曾在微软和 DraftKings 工作过，他表示，今年在担任软件工程师和数据科学实习生时，公司鼓励他尽可能多地使用人工智能。 他没有完成基本的软件工程工作和制作票证，而是将大部分时间花在计划上，然后花更少的时间提示 Claude 编写代码。 他怀念编写代码的时光，但他的工作范围已经扩大了。 “我的项目非常大，而且具有良好的商业价值，”他说。 “更多的是思考如何解决更大的问题。”

米兹拉知道，在明年寻找毕业后工作时，他正在积累令人印象深刻的经验，可以与未来的雇主交谈，但他仍然担心职业生涯早期的就业市场状况。 科技公司正在与工程面试中的人工智能作弊作斗争，并且有很多准备工作可以跟上不断变化的期望和评估。 “这肯定会让事情变得更加困难，因为现在每个人都精通代码。”

随着人工智能越来越多地触及大学经历并渗透到更多的工作日，人们越来越担心过度依赖会侵蚀批判性思维。 大学对于是否应该或如何加强模拟学习几乎没有达成共识，而公司正在努力寻找审查员工使用人工智能的最佳方法。 早期研究不断提出人工智能对我们的创造性思维和推理能力的长期影响的问题。 陷入不确定性之中，年轻人急切地寻求最有可能找到全职工作的技能和安全感。 但这些工作的需求升级的速度可能比年轻工人对自己的判断更有信心的速度要快。

最好的训练场还是来自于干活。 想要培训未来人才如何使用人工智能的管理者应该问自己：“这项任务是否有助于提高这个人的判断力？” 薄荷糖说。 “这些经验是否足以取代他们在开始实习时所获得的经验？” 感谢2026年实习生班，明年的暑期实习生可能会走进看起来截然不同的工作场所。
